For t>=d the weighted slope is G(d,t)=exp(cd)[f(d)-cU(d)]+integral_d^t exp(cs)f'(s)ds. It decreases strictly in t, and at fixed t its d derivative is c(b-c)exp(cd)U(d)>0. Thus G(d,d_end)<0<G(d,d) in the two-peak regime with finite endpoint and d<t2(d)<d_end; the limiting height is f(d_end)/c=U(d_end)<U(t0). On constant-rate reaches the weighted derivative crosses zero at most once and f, U and the downstream solution vanish at infinity. The lag integral for U/f has a positive expanding domain and nondecreasing integrand by nondecreasing hazard, giving strict monotonicity, all right-derivative regimes, and no extra extremum at either boundary. Moving the interface later strictly lowers the profile after the later interface, hence strictly lowers the downstream peak. At t0 the peak is higher than the reference; at an infinite endpoint the upper bound U(d)+f(d)/c tends to zero. Continuity then proves the unique tie and full global-maximizer comparison.
